Couple tips:

Microsoft is a shit company to work for, ask anyone. As a rule of thumb, any employer that you'd put on your resume sucks to work for. Amazon, Facebook, you've probably heard about Google's recent problems.

When an employer says they need a degree, they don't. That interviewer just doesn't have the authority to hire you without a degree, but someone there does, and the person who cares about making money isn't going to turn you down if you can make him money.

There are a couple sure-fire ways to get employed, as long as you're under 30 and have no felonies. One is to do volunteer work, prove your value, and then ask for a job. As an example, find a team that's trying to win an x-prize spin-off and produce some software that helps their project. As a more specific example, I programmed a GUI to display an already made object model of a satellite and the information it was transmitting. They had previously been using a CLI, but when I showed them what I had made they offered me a job. It took me about 3 hours to do with Unity3D. It might not usually be that easy, but that's the basic idea. Prove your value and its a matter of how much do they want to pay you, not if they want to hire you.

The other way is to start your own business. Website building is the easiest, WP takes like 5 minutes to set up and you'll get $300 for that shit, although its pretty saturated they might not be paying $300 anymore, been a while since I was doing that. Other opportunities include computer repair, manufacturing cheap wood weight racks, FOSS that you get BTC donations for, etc. Think outside the box, the opportunities are endless.

Finally, when you're looking for a job, its about who you know, not what you know. That has always been the case, and LinkedIn didn't change anything the way we thought it would. The "put your resume on the internet" model works for companies that are scaling up, but that's not most hiring. Most hiring is done when an employer realizes a very specific new way to make money, and they usually only realize that after they've been sold on the idea by the person they're going to hire.

To really understand that mindset, try to start your own business and think about the ways you can grow it. If you're doing WP websites, as an example, maybe you could automate the process with some software, or maybe you could hire more people to make websites, or maybe you could put an ad in the newspaper. That's the easy, uncommon, internet resume type of hiring. The first guy you'll hire, though? The guy who shows up and says he can offer you a 100s of website contracts for a small commission. You're not going to give a shit about his qualifications, you might not even care if he's a 90 year old felon, because it doesn't matter how you get that contract, you're getting paid either way. Its the sort of thing you didn't even know you could hire someone to do. Its hard to understand until you've been there.
